title: The Workbench table count is 92 in version 6 and 93 in the Ownership Map
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Target Architecture v6.pptx (slides 11 and 12); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx (sheet Tables); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: Target Architecture v6 slide 11 (data architecture: four tiers, one read path), callout '92 Workbench tables, 30 views, 122 dictionary objects and 1,366 dictionary fields'; Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables, 93 rows
description: Version 6 states 92 Workbench tables: 4 extension tables and 88 retained tables, with 30 views, 122 dictionary objects and 1,366 fields. The Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables carries 93 rows: 87 business or Workbench tables assigned to the 19 services plus 6 platform library tables (feature_flag, feature_flag_change, idempotency_key, outbox_event, outbox_delivery, processed_event) owned by PLT. The two readings differ by one table and by the way the library tables are counted; slide 11 of the deck is kept word for word, so the deck states 92 while the Map and the physical schema work carry 93.
evidence: Target Architecture v6 slide 11 text box 16 reads '92 Workbench tables, 30 views, 122 dictionary objects and 1,366 dictionary fields'; its Tier 3 shape reads '4 extension tables' and its Tier 4 shape reads '88 Workbench tables'. Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables has one header row and 93 data rows: P1 18, P2 3, P3 15, P4 5, P5 12, P6 3, P7 6, P8 1, P9 3, P10 8, S2 1, S3 1, S4 2, S5 2, S6 2, S7 1, S8 1, S9 3, PLT 6.
proposed: State the target count once, as the Ownership Map count of 93 rows (87 Workbench tables and 6 platform library tables created in every schema), and record 92 as the version 6 monolith count that the physical schema work replaces.

title: The shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 has no topic settings
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 20, 22, 28 and 41); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R4)
section: Architecture v5 slide 20 (what every service does, EVT line), slide 22 (how an event travels), slide 28 (the decision log), slide 41 (service catalogue, topic column)
description: Every service publishes DecisionRecorded to rwb.decision-record.v1 and rwb-decision consumes it into the central ledger within five minutes. No source gives the partitions, replication factor, retention, key, schema subject or ACLs of that topic; the per-service topics rwb.<short>.events.v1 carry 12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention and key caseId on slide 9 of the same extract, and those settings are not stated for the shared topic.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 41 lists rwb.<name>.events.v1 for each of the 19 services and names rwb.decision-record.v1 only in slide 20 ('DecisionRecorded -> rwb.decision-record.v1 (ledger in rwb-decision)') and slide 28 ('rwb-decision reads rwb.decision-record.v1 into the ledger within 5 minutes'). Slide 9 gives the Kafka settings for the service topics only. Rules R4 names the shared topic and no settings.
proposed: Set the partitions, replication factor, retention, key, subject naming and ACLs of rwb.decision-record.v1 with the Kafka platform team, and publish them with the topic catalogue.

title: gateway-bff and the partner gateway have no owner code, no wave and no service row
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 8, 20 and 41); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx (sheet Services)
section: Architecture v5 slide 8 (system architecture), slide 20 (gateway-bff, shared platform) and slide 41 (the 19 services); Ownership Map v1 sheet Services, 19 rows
description: gateway-bff and the partner gateway are part of the edge and are counted outside the 19 services. Architecture v5 gives gateway-bff a contract (browser entry, session in Redis, one hop to the owner, ACE Common sign-in) and the partner gateway FAPI 2.0 in the DMZ, but no source gives either an Ownership Map code, a wave, a schema, a topic or a task queue. The service epics in R5.1 name RWB-PLT-EDGE as the epic that delivers the edge, and no story inside it owns gateway-bff in any source read for this work package.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 8 notes read 'the Recovery gateway-bff (Spring Cloud Gateway, session in Redis, sign-in through ACE Common)' and 'Partners use the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) that fronts rwb-partner'. Slide 20 gives gateway-bff the label 'shared platform' with no service code. Ownership Map v1 sheet Services lists 19 rows, P1 to P10 and S1 to S9, and no edge row.
proposed: Name the owner of gateway-bff and of the partner gateway in the edge epic RWB-PLT-EDGE, and state whether each has a schema, a topic or a task queue (this work package assumes none).

title: A service's first epic in version 6 differs from its wave in Architecture v5
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Target Architecture v6.pptx (slide 15); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slide 38); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx (sheet Services, column Wave)
section: Target Architecture v6 slide 15 (what each epic adds); Architecture v5 slide 38 (getting there: services arrive with the epics that need them); Ownership Map v1 sheet Services, column Wave
description: Version 6 slide 15 attributes features to epics: P8 matching in E2 and posting in E4, S2 foundations in E2 and settlement in E3, S5 record in E3 and auction in E4, S4 notices in E2 and end to end in E5, S6 data in E5 and screens in E6, S8 screening in E2 and end to end in E7, S7 in E6, S9 panel in E6 and scoring in E7, S1 and S3 in E4. Architecture v5 slide 38 and the Ownership Map give one wave per service: P8, S2, S5 and S8 in wave 2, S1, S3, S4 and S6 in wave 3, S7 and S9 in wave 4. A service therefore first appears in a different epic under the two readings, which changes the wave a story belongs to and the wave band of the diagram.
evidence: Target Architecture v6 slide 15, column Added, reads for E2 'P8 matching skeleton ... S2 treatment record; S4 notice approval; S8 deviation screening', for E3 'S5 asset record ...', for E4 'S1 route decision ... S3 guarantee ... S5 auction rounds ... P8 posting', for E5 'S4 litigation end to end ... S6 lot data and data room', for E6 'S6 debt sale screens ... S7 write-off ... S9 partner panel'. Architecture v5 slide 38 gives 'Wave 2 · Epics 2-3 +4 services P8, S2, S5, S8' and 'Wave 3 · Epics 4-5 +4 services S1, S3, S4, S6'. Ownership Map v1 sheet Services gives wave 2 to P8, S2, S5, S8; wave 3 to S1, S3, S4, S6; wave 4 to S7, S9.
proposed: Resolve in favour of the Architecture v5 wave map (R-PREC 1): the wave of a service is the Ownership Map wave; version 6 slide 15 keeps the features each epic adds and the deck states that a service's wave, not its epic of first use, fixes its delivery band.

title: No source sizes the deployment slots for 38 deployments across four environments
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Target Architecture v6.pptx (slide 14); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 33 and 38)
section: Target Architecture v6 slide 14 (environments and the release path, column Notes); Architecture v5 slide 33 (scale only what is busy) and slide 38 (wave 0)
description: Version 6 counts slots per environment: DEV four planned and one available, SIT two planned and one available (DL35), UAT shared with the collection squad, PROD on the shared ACE AKS clusters. Architecture v5 makes each of the 19 services an api and a worker deployment, about 38 deployments at rest, plus Temporal, Kafka clients, the gateway and observability. No source states whether the planned slots hold 38 deployments per environment, how the namespaces and quotas are split between the environments, or when the missing slots arrive.
evidence: Target Architecture v6 slide 14 rows DEV and SIT read 'Four slots planned, one available (DL35)' and 'Two slots planned, one available (DL35)'. Architecture v5 slide 33 notes read 'about 38 small deployments at rest (most workers idle at minimum), one Helm chart and one pipeline template'. Slide 38 makes wave 0 the enabler with the template, the Helm chart and the 19 schemas and logins. No slide gives a slot count for the target.
proposed: Confirm the slots and quotas per environment for 38 deployments plus the platform components, and record the date each missing slot arrives against wave 0.

title: The repository model for the 19 services is not stated
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Target Architecture v6.pptx (slides 3, 4 and 6); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 33 and 38); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.1)
section: Target Architecture v6 slide 3 (constraint 'Built on ACE: one service, one repository, one front end'), slide 4 principle 2 and slide 6 (the modular monolith); Architecture v5 slide 33 note 'one Helm chart and one pipeline template'; Rules R5.1 epic RWB-PLT-TPL 'service template and repositories'
description: Version 6 fixes one repository for the Workbench. Architecture v5 says one Helm chart and one pipeline template per service and names the service template and repositories as the wave 0 platform epic, which reads as a repository per service, but no source states whether the target uses one repository per service, one repository with 19 modules, or a mixed model. The answer changes the pipeline gates, the code owners and the boundary test of every service.
evidence: Target Architecture v6 slide 3 row 'Built on ACE' reads 'The Workbench is a module of ACE: one service, one repository, one front end'; slide 4 principle 2 reads 'One service, one repository, one front end'. Architecture v5 slide 33 notes read 'one Helm chart and one pipeline template' as the cost of 19 services and do not name repositories. Rules R5.1 lists 'RWB-PLT-TPL: service template and repositories' with no count.
proposed: State the repository and pipeline model in the service template specification, with the code owners and the boundary test that follow from it.

title: The Temporal cluster, namespace and workflow kit are owned by a role, not by an owner code
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 23, 24 and 39); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slide 12); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: Architecture v5 slide 23 (Temporal in five layers), slide 24 (Temporal at runtime) and slide 39 (decision 3, owner Platform team, ACE team); Temporal and Drools design slide 12 (L1 to L3 owned by the platform team); Ownership Map v1 sheets Workflows and activities and Jobs
description: Layers L1 to L3 of the Temporal layer are owned by 'the platform team': the cluster, the persistence database, the namespaces and the versioned workflow kit. No Ownership Map code owns them: the Map assigns the 15 workflows to service and PLT codes, and the platform jobs JOB-21 and JOB-22 to PLT, with no row for the cluster, the namespace rwb-recovery or the kit. Rules R5.1 gives the epics RWB-PLT-WF for the workflow platform and RWB-PLT-LIB for shared libraries, which is the nearest the story plan comes to an owner.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 23 labels L1, L2 and L3 'platform team'; slide 39 decision 3 reads 'Owner: Platform team, ACE team'. Temporal and Drools design slide 12 labels L1 to L3 'platform team'. ownership.json has 15 workflow rows (P3, P5, P6, P7, P10, S1 to S9, PLT) and 22 job rows, of which JOB-05, JOB-11, JOB-21 and JOB-22 are PLT, and no cluster, namespace or kit row.
proposed: Name the PLT epic or story that owns the cluster, the namespace and the workflow kit (RWB-PLT-WF for the platform and RWB-PLT-LIB for the kit in this deck), and record whether the running service is run by the platform team or by ACE.
